answer: Use a warm-up delay curve: new identities get tight rate limits until they sustain low-burst traffic across spaced windows. A velvet-rope delay holds first privileged calls until several windows pass without gaps, forcing each fake identity to run live. A ridge of rolling averages resets the clock on sharp spikes. Attackers pay wall-clock time and one continuous stream per identity to reach the same summit, so mass Sybil creation needs parallel compute and scheduling.
